evals.name: pretooluse-hook-demo
evals.prompt: I'm teaching Claude Code hooks next week. Make me a live demo animation of PreToolUse hooks — students should see where the hook is wired, the script, what happens when Claude tries a blocked command. Use projects/file-browser in this repo, it has a real guard-bash hook.
evals.expected_output: Two local HTML files in projects/file-browser: <slug>-live-demo.html (animated Claude Code IDE: sidebar tree, main pane switching between Claude terminal and file viewer, bottom shell) showing .claude/settings.json and .claude/hooks/guard-bash.sh opened from the real tree, the hook run standalone in the shell with its real BLOCKED output, then a prompt to Claude whose Bash call is blocked with the hook's stderr; and the deep-dive explainer HTML, linked from the demo's player bar. Timeline JSON built via build_demo.py. Nothing published.
assertions: Deliverable is a self-contained local HTML file written into the project root (its only external resource is a Google Fonts stylesheet, no external JS); nothing was published as an Artifact
The IDE replica has all three panes: a sidebar file tree, a main pane that switches between the Claude Code terminal and a file viewer, and a bottom shell terminal

Every file opened in the animation exists at that path in projects/file-browser and its shown content matches the file on disk (byte-identical up to the first 600 lines; a longer file is truncated with an explicit … N more lines marker, never abridged silently or renumbered)
Every shell command output shown reproduces when the command is re-run; any elision is marked with an ellipsis
A Claude turn is shown with a typed prompt, at least one tool-call line (⏺ Name(arg) + ⎿ result line), streamed prose, and a ❋ done line
The Claude pane reproduces the real app's chrome: ❯ composer, status line with project name + [model · effort] + usage bar, and the ▶▶ mode line
Captions narrate each beat, and the player offers play/pause, step, and a draggable scrub bar
The player bar has a Deep dive link whose relative href resolves to the deep-dive HTML the tech-deep-dive-artifact skill wrote in the same folder
The hand-off states which Claude turns were captured from a real run (with the run.jsonl path) vs authored
The animation opens .claude/settings.json and highlights/scrolls to the PreToolUse hook entry (the Bash matcher → guard-bash.sh)
The animation opens .claude/hooks/guard-bash.sh and highlights the exit 2 / block() mechanism
The hook's real BLOCKED stderr text ('BLOCKED by guard-bash hook: …') appears verbatim, either from a standalone shell run or as the tool-result of the blocked Bash call
The Claude turn shows the dangerous Bash call being blocked (warn-styled result carrying Claude Code's 'PreToolUse:Bash hook error' prefix if captured), not executed

evals.name: path-scoped-rules-demo
evals.prompt: show my students how path-scoped rules work in claude code (the .claude/rules/*.md files with paths: frontmatter) — I want an animation they can watch, not slides. demo project is projects/file-browser
evals.expected_output: Two local HTML files in projects/file-browser: the animated demo (Claude Code IDE replica) that opens a real .claude/rules/*.md file showing its paths: frontmatter, contrasts with an always-on rule, shows a negative case (non-matching Read → rule not loaded) and a positive case (matching Read → rule loaded), then a Claude edit that obeys the rule; and the deep-dive explainer HTML linked from the demo. Real file contents from disk; captions per beat; nothing published.
assertions: Deliverable is a self-contained local HTML file written into the project root (its only external resource is a Google Fonts stylesheet, no external JS); nothing was published as an Artifact
The IDE replica has all three panes: a sidebar file tree, a main pane that switches between the Claude Code terminal and a file viewer, and a bottom shell terminal

Every file opened in the animation exists at that path in projects/file-browser and its shown content matches the file on disk (byte-identical up to the first 600 lines; a longer file is truncated with an explicit … N more lines marker, never abridged silently or renumbered)
Every shell command output shown reproduces when the command is re-run; any elision is marked with an ellipsis
A Claude turn is shown with a typed prompt, at least one tool-call line (⏺ Name(arg) + ⎿ result line), streamed prose, and a ❋ done line
The Claude pane reproduces the real app's chrome: ❯ composer, status line with project name + [model · effort] + usage bar, and the ▶▶ mode line
Captions narrate each beat, and the player offers play/pause, step, and a draggable scrub bar
The player bar has a Deep dive link whose relative href resolves to the deep-dive HTML the tech-deep-dive-artifact skill wrote in the same folder
The hand-off states which Claude turns were captured from a real run (with the run.jsonl path) vs authored
The animation opens a real .claude/rules/*.md file from file-browser that has a `paths:` frontmatter and highlights that frontmatter
The demo contrasts a path-scoped rule with an always-on rule (no paths:)
A negative case is shown: Claude reads a file outside the rule's globs and the rule is not loaded
A positive case is shown: Claude reads/edits a file matching the rule's paths glob and the rule's effect is visible
